## codegraph
# Codegraph — code intelligence over an indexed knowledge graph

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol, edge, and file in
the workspace — pre-computed structure you would otherwise re-derive by
reading files (cached intelligence: thousands of parse/trace decisions you
don't pay to re-reason each run). Reads are sub-millisecond; the index lags
writes by ~1s through the file watcher. Reach for it BEFORE *and* while
writing or editing code — not just for questions: one call returns the
verbatim source PLUS who calls it and what it affects, so you edit with the
blast radius in view. More accurate context, in far fewer tokens and
round-trips than reading files yourself.

## One tool: codegraph_explore — use it instead of reading files

There is a single tool, `codegraph_explore`, and it is Read-equivalent. It
takes either a natural-language question or a bag of symbol/file names and
returns the **verbatim, line-numbered source** of the relevant symbols
grouped by file — the same `<n>\t<line>` shape `Read` gives you, safe to
`Edit` from — PLUS the call path among them (including dynamic-dispatch hops
like callbacks, React re-render, and JSX children that grep can't follow) and
a blast-radius summary of what depends on them.

Whether you're answering "how does X work" or implementing a change (fixing a
bug, adding a feature), call `codegraph_explore` before you Read. ONE call
usually answers the whole question. Codegraph IS the pre-built search index —
so running your own grep + read loop, or delegating the lookup to a separate
file-reading sub-task/agent, repeats work codegraph already did and costs more
for the same answer. A direct codegraph answer is typically one to a few
calls; a grep/read exploration is dozens.

## How to query

- **Almost any question — "how does X work", architecture, a bug, "what/where is X", or surveying an area** → `codegraph_explore` with a natural-language question or the relevant names. ONE capped call returns the verbatim source grouped by file; most often the ONLY call y… [truncated]

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

98	func (c *Cache) SetWithTTL(_ context.Context, key string, value any, ttl time.Duration) {

100		size := estimateSize(value)
101	
102		// Check if item already exists to avoid double counting.
103		if _, exists := c.data.Load(key); exists {
104			c.data.Delete(key)
105		} else {
106			// Only increment if this is a new key.
107			(&c.itemCount).Add(1)
108		}
109	
110		c.data.Store(key, item{
111			value:      value,
112			expiration: time.Now().Add(ttl),
113			size:       size,
114		})

116		// If we're over the max items, clean up old items.
117		if c.config.MaxItems > 0 && (&c.itemCount).Load() > int64(c.config.MaxItems) {

124		value, ok := c.data.Load(key)
125		if !ok {
126			return nil, false
127		}
128	
129		itm, ok := value.(item)
130		if !ok {
131			// If the value is not of type item, it means it was corrupted or not set correctly.
132			c.data.Delete(key)
133			return nil, false
134		}
135		if time.Now().After(itm.expiration) {
136			c.data.Delete(key)
137			(&c.itemCount).Add(-1)
138	
139			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
140				c.config.OnEviction(key, itm.value)
141			}
142	
143			return nil, false
144		}
145	
146		return itm.value, true
147	}
148	
149	// Delete removes a value from the cache.
150	func (c *Cache) Delete(_ context.Context, key string) {
151		if value, loaded := c.data.LoadAndDelete(key); loaded {
152			(&c.itemCount).Add(-1)
153	
154			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
155				if itm, ok := value.(item); ok {
156					c.config.OnEviction(key, itm.value)
157				}
158			}
159		}
160	}
161	
162	// Clear removes all values from the cache.
163	func (c *Cache) Clear(_ context.Context) {
164		count := 0
165		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
166			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
167				itm, ok := value.(item)
168				if ok {
169					if keyStr, ok := key.(string); ok {
170						c.config.OnEviction(keyStr, itm.value)
171					}
172				}
173			}
174			c.data.Delete(key)
175			count++
176			return true
177		})
178		(&c.itemCount).Store(0)
179	}
180	
181	// Size returns the number of items in the cache.
182	func (c *Cache) Size() int64 {
183		return (&c.itemCount).Load()
184	}

187	func (c *Cache) Close() error {
188		select {
189		case <-c.stopChan:
190			// Already closed
191			return nil
192		default:
193			close(c.stopChan)
194			<-c.closedChan // Wait for cleanup goroutine to exit
195			return nil
196		}
197	}

199	// cleanupLoop periodically cleans up expired items.
200	func (c *Cache) cleanupLoop() {
201		ticker := time.NewTicker(c.config.CleanupInterval)
202		defer func() {
203			ticker.Stop()
204			close(c.closedChan)
205		}()
206	
207		for {
208			select {
209			case <-ticker.C:
210				c.cleanup()
211			case <-c.stopChan:
212				return
213			}
214		}
215	}
216	
217	// cleanup removes expired items.
218	func (c *Cache) cleanup() {
219		evicted := make(map[string]any)
220		count := 0
221	
222		c.data.Range(func(key, value any) bool {
223			itm, ok := value.(item)

235				}
236			}
237			return true
238		})
239	
240		if count > 0 {
241			(&c.itemCount).Add(-int64(count))
242	
243			// Call eviction callbacks outside the loop to avoid blocking the range
244			if c.config.OnEviction != nil {
245				for k, v := range evicted {
246					c.config.OnEviction(k, v)
247				}
248			}
249		}
250	}

## codegraph
# Codegraph — code intelligence over an indexed knowledge graph

Codegraph is a SQLite knowledge graph of every symbol, edge, and file in
the workspace — pre-computed structure you would otherwise re-derive by
reading files (cached intelligence: thousands of parse/trace decisions you
don't pay to re-reason each run). Reads are sub-millisecond; the index lags
writes by ~1s through the file watcher. Reach for it BEFORE *and* while
writing or editing code — not just for questions: one call returns the
verbatim source PLUS who calls it and what it affects, so you edit with the
blast radius in view. More accurate context, in far fewer tokens and
round-trips than reading files yourself.

## One tool: codegraph_explore — use it instead of reading files

There is a single tool, `codegraph_explore`, and it is Read-equivalent. It
takes either a natural-language question or a bag of symbol/file names and
returns the **verbatim, line-numbered source** of the relevant symbols
grouped by file — the same `<n>\t<line>` shape `Read` gives you, safe to
`Edit` from — PLUS the call path among them (including dynamic-dispatch hops
like callbacks, React re-render, and JSX children that grep can't follow) and
a blast-radius summary of what depends on them.

Whether you're answering "how does X work" or implementing a change (fixing a
bug, adding a feature), call `codegraph_explore` before you Read. ONE call
usually answers the whole question. Codegraph IS the pre-built search index —
so running your own grep + read loop, or delegating the lookup to a separate
file-reading sub-task/agent, repeats work codegraph already did and costs more
for the same answer. A direct codegraph answer is typically one to a few
calls; a grep/read exploration is dozens.

## How to query

- **Almost any question — "how does X work", architecture, a bug, "what/where is X", or surveying an area** → `codegraph_explore` with a natural-language question or the relevant names. ONE capped call returns the verbatim source grouped by file; most often the ONLY call y… [truncated]

71	func (h *SSEHub) Subscribe(userID int32, role store.Role) *SSEClient {
72		c := &SSEClient{
73			// Buffer a few events so a slow client doesn't block broadcasting.
74			events: make(chan []byte, 32),
75			userID: userID,
76			role:   role,
77		}
78		h.mu.Lock()
79		if h.closed {
80			close(c.events)
81		} else {
82			h.clients[c] = struct{}{}
83		}
84		h.mu.Unlock()
85		return c
86	}

90		h.mu.Lock()
91		if _, ok := h.clients[c]; ok {
92			delete(h.clients, c)
93			close(c.events)
94		}
95		h.mu.Unlock()
96	}

99	func (h *SSEHub) Close() {
100		h.mu.Lock()
101		defer h.mu.Unlock()
102		if h.closed {
103			return
104		}
105		h.closed = true
106		for c := range h.clients {
107			delete(h.clients, c)
108			close(c.events)
109		}

114	// to avoid blocking the broadcaster.
115	func (h *SSEHub) Broadcast(event *SSEEvent) {
116		data := event.JSON()
117		if len(data) == 0 {
118			return
119		}
120		h.mu.RLock()
121		defer h.mu.RUnlock()
122		for c := range h.clients {
123			if !c.canReceive(event) {
124				continue
125			}
126			select {
127			case c.events <- data:
128			default:
129				// Drop event for slow client to avoid blocking.
130			}
131		}
132	}

139			return true

32	// handleSSE handles the SSE connection for live memo refresh.
33	// Authentication is done via Bearer token in the Authorization header.
34	func handleSSE(c *echo.Context, hub *SSEHub, authenticator *auth.Authenticator) error {
35		// Authenticate the request.
36		authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Authorization")
37		result := authenticator.Authenticate(c.Request().Context(), authHeader)
38		if result == nil {
39			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
40		}
41		userID, role := getSSEClientIdentity(result)
42		if userID == 0 {
43			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
44		}
45	
46		// Set SSE headers.
47		w := c.Response()
48		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
49		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
50		w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
51		w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no") // Disable nginx buffering
52		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
53	
54		// Flush headers immediately.
55		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
56			f.Flush()
57		}
58	
59		// Subscribe to the hub.
60		client := hub.Subscribe(userID, role)
61		defer hub.Unsubscribe(client)
62	
63		// Create a ticker for heartbeat pings.
64		heartbeat := time.NewTicker(sseHeartbeatInterval)
65		defer heartbeat.Stop()
66	
67		ctx := c.Request().Context()
68	
69		slog.Debug("SSE client connected", "userID", userID)
70	
71		// Send an initial comment so clients and dev proxies observe the stream
72		// immediately instead of waiting for the first heartbeat or data event.
73		if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": connected\n\n"); err != nil {
74			return nil
75		}
76		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
77			f.Flush()
78		}
79	
80		for {
81			select {
82			case <-ctx.Done():
83				// Client disconnected.
84				slog.Debug("SSE client disconnected", "userID", userID)
85				return nil
86	
87			case data, ok := <-client.events:
88				if !ok {
89					// Channel closed, client was unsubscribed.
90					return nil
91				}
92				// Write SSE event.
93				if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", data); err != nil {
94					return nil
95				}
96				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
97					f.Flush()
98				}
99	
100			case <-heartbeat.C:
101				// Send a heartbeat comment to keep the connection alive.
102				if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
103					return nil
104				}
105				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
106					f.Flush()
107				}
108			}
109		}
110	}

112	func getSSEClientIdentity(result *auth.AuthResult) (int32, store.Role) {
113		if result == nil {

115		}
116		if result.Claims != nil {
117			return result.Claims.UserID, store.Role(result.Claims.Role)
118		}
119		if result.User != nil {
120			return result.User.ID, result.User.Role
121		}
122		return 0, store.RoleUser

33	// Authentication is done via Bearer token in the Authorization header.
34	func handleSSE(c *echo.Context, hub *SSEHub, authenticator *auth.Authenticator) error {
35		// Authenticate the request.
36		authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Authorization")
37		result := authenticator.Authenticate(c.Request().Context(), authHeader)
38		if result == nil {
39			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
40		}
41		userID, role := getSSEClientIdentity(result)
42		if userID == 0 {
43			return c.JSON(http.StatusUnauthorized, map[string]string{"error": "authentication required"})
44		}
45	
46		// Set SSE headers.
47		w := c.Response()
48		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
49		w.Header().Set("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
50		w.Header().Set("Connection", "keep-alive")
51		w.Header().Set("X-Accel-Buffering", "no") // Disable nginx buffering
52		w.WriteHeader(http.StatusOK)
53	
54		// Flush headers immediately.
55		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
56			f.Flush()
57		}
58	
59		// Subscribe to the hub.
60		client := hub.Subscribe(userID, role)
61		defer hub.Unsubscribe(client)
62	
63		// Create a ticker for heartbeat pings.
64		heartbeat := time.NewTicker(sseHeartbeatInterval)
65		defer heartbeat.Stop()
66	
67		ctx := c.Request().Context()
68	
69		slog.Debug("SSE client connected", "userID", userID)
70	
71		// Send an initial comment so clients and dev proxies observe the stream
72		// immediately instead of waiting for the first heartbeat or data event.
73		if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": connected\n\n"); err != nil {
74			return nil
75		}
76		if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
77			f.Flush()
78		}
79	
80		for {
81			select {
82			case <-ctx.Done():
83				// Client disconnected.
84				slog.Debug("SSE client disconnected", "userID", userID)
85				return nil
86	
87			case data, ok := <-client.events:
88				if !ok {
89					// Channel closed, client was unsubscribed.
90					return nil
91				}
92				// Write SSE event.
93				if _, err := fmt.Fprintf(w, "data: %s\n\n", data); err != nil {
94					return nil
95				}
96				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
97					f.Flush()
98				}
99	
100			case <-heartbeat.C:
101				// Send a heartbeat comment to keep the connection alive.
102				if _, err := fmt.Fprint(w, ": heartbeat\n\n"); err != nil {
103					return nil
104				}
105				if f, ok := w.(http.Flusher); ok {
106					f.Flush()
107				}
108			}
109		}

29	func (r *Runner) Run(ctx context.Context) {
30		ticker := time.NewTicker(runnerInterval)
31		defer ticker.Stop()
32	
33		for {
34			select {
35			case <-ticker.C:
36				r.RunOnce(ctx)
37			case <-ctx.Done():
38				return
39			}
40		}
41	}

43	func (r *Runner) RunOnce(ctx context.Context) {
44		r.CheckAndPresign(ctx)
45	}

47	func (r *Runner) CheckAndPresign(ctx context.Context) {
48		instanceStorageSetting, err := r.Store.GetInstanceStorageSetting(ctx)
49		if err != nil {
50			return
51		}
52	
53		s3StorageType := storepb.AttachmentStorageType_S3
54		// Limit attachments to a reasonable batch size
55		const batchSize = 100
56		offset := 0
57	
58		for {
59			limit := batchSize
60			attachments, err := r.Store.ListAttachments(ctx, &store.FindAttachment{
61				GetBlob:     false,
62				StorageType: &s3StorageType,
63				Limit:       &limit,
64				Offset:      &offset,
65			})
66			if err != nil {
67				slog.Error("Failed to list attachments for presigning", "error", err)
68				return
69			}
70	
71			// Break if no more attachments
72			if len(attachments) == 0 {
73				break
74			}
75	
76			// Process batch of attachments
77			presignCount := 0
78			for _, attachment := range attachments {
79				payload := cloneAttachmentPayload(attachment.Payload)
80				s3ObjectPayload := payload.GetS3Object()
81				if s3ObjectPayload == nil {
82					continue
83				}
84	
85				if s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime != nil {
86					// Skip if the presigned URL is still valid for the next 4 days.
87					// The expiration time is set to 5 days.
88					if time.Now().Before(s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime.AsTime().Add(4 * 24 * time.Hour)) {
89						continue
90					}
91				}
92	
93				s3Config := instanceStorageSetting.GetS3Config()
94				if s3ObjectPayload.S3Config != nil {
95					s3Config = s3ObjectPayload.S3Config
96				}
97				if s3Config == nil {
98					slog.Error("S3 config is not found")
99					continue
100				}
101	
102				s3Client, err := s3.NewClient(ctx, s3Config)
103				if err != nil {
104					slog.Error("Failed to create S3 client", "error", err)
105					continue
106				}
107	
108				presignURL, err := s3Client.PresignGetObject(ctx, s3ObjectPayload.Key)
109				if err != nil {
110					slog.Error("Failed to presign URL", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
111					continue
112				}
113	
114				s3ObjectPayload.S3Config = s3Config
115				s3ObjectPayload.LastPresignedTime = timestamppb.New(time.Now())
116				if err := r.Store.UpdateAttachment(ctx, &store.UpdateAttachment{
117					ID:        attachment.ID,
118					Reference: &presignURL,
119					Payload:   payload,
120				}); err != nil {
121					slog.Error("Failed to update attachment", "error", err, "attachmentID", attachment.ID)
122					continue
123				}
124				presignCount++
125			}
126	
127			slog.Info("Presigned batch of S3 attachments", "batchSize", len(attachments), "presigned", presignCount)
128	
129			// Move to next batch
130			offset += len(attachments)
131		}
132	}

135		if payload == nil {

137		}
138		cloned, ok := proto.Clone(payload).(*storepb.AttachmentPayload)
139		if !ok {
140			return nil
141		}
142		return cloned
143	}
